Rule: A.1 99) 'Implementor-defined exception conditions, EC-IMP-xxx (specification and meaning of xxx). This item is optional. This item, if provided by the implementor, shall be documented' -> §14.6.13.1.6 Table 13 row 'EC-IMP-*suffix* (implementor specifies *suffix*) | Imp | Level-3 implementor-defined exception condition'. Code: ExceptionCatalog accepts EC-IMP-<any valid suffix> as an open family (like EC-USER-*), level 3, parent EC-IMP, fatality Imp which this implementation treats as FATAL; the runtime raises no EC-IMP-* itself. Probe p99 (>>TURN EC-ALL CHECKING ON; RAISE EXCEPTION EC-IMP-WIBBLE): compiles, 'abnormal run-unit termination: EC-IMP-WIBBLE (fatal): raised by RAISE and not resumed', exit 1. So the implementation DOES make a determination — every suffix is a valid name, meaning 'a user-raisable fatal condition the runtime never sets' — and it is undocumented => DIVERGES (silent). And if the intended answer is 'not provided', accepting an arbitrary EC-IMP-suffix is an under-rejection: Table 13 makes the suffix set the implementor's to SPECIFY, so a suffix never specified names no exception condition. No owning note (grep item 99 / EC-IMP-suffix in kb/Work: none). cite.py --check 14.6.13.1.6 'EC-IMP-*suffix* (implementor specifies *suffix*)' -> OK §14.6.13.1.6; 'Level-3 implementor-defined exception condition' -> OK.

Rule: A.1 113) 'Life cycle for objects (timing and algorithm for taking part in continued execution). This item is required. This item need not be documented in the implementor's user documentation.' -> §9.3.14.3 'An instance object is destroyed either when it is determined that the object cannot take part in the continued execution of the run unit, or when the run unit terminates, whichever occurs first. The timing and algorithm for the mechanism that determines whether or not an instance object can take part in the continued execution of the run unit is implementor-defined.' Documentation not required (audit register documented=False), so the absent §7 row is correct. Behaviour: a COBOL object is a managed .NET instance deriving CobolObject; reachability is decided by the .NET tracing garbage collector (the NOTE's 'garbage collection'), timing nondeterministic as the rule permits; the only object-owned resource with observable destruction (a per-object instance file, §9.1.4) is closed by a re-armed finalizer on collection, with CobolFile.CloseAll() at run-unit termination as the 'whichever occurs first' backstop.
